annotations.title: Smallest condition changes that admit plans

description: Use this when: search finds no plan or too few plans and the user wants to know which condition to loosen and by how much. Do not use this when: plans already match (use search or check_conditions). When no plan, or too few plans, meet every required condition: for each condition the user can change, returns the smallest change that lets at least one plan meet everything (for example the monthly budget needed, the concurrency available, or one exit-IP country to drop) and the plans it admits with their monthly cost. Also lists plans that fail only because a condition is not stated on the official pages, with the pages checked and the check date, so the user can confirm with the provider.

ai_extraction_pages.description: How many of the pages need their fields extracted by an AI model (from a prompt or a schema, or automatically) without writing selectors. Each page counts in one of the two extraction fields.

billing_types.description: Acceptable billing: monthly_subscription (A plan with a fixed fee (or minimum commitment) billed every month.) annual_subscription (A plan paid for a year at a time.) pay_as_you_go (No plan fee; a price per unit of use, billed after use or drawn from a balance topped up with any amount.) prepaid_credits (A fixed-size credit pack bought before use, usually with an expiry.) Free plans always qualify.

browser_seconds_per_page.description: Browser time per page in seconds, for headless-browser products billed by time. Every plan must then serve pages that take this long: a hosted browser does, a request-based API only when one request may run that long.

data_regions.description: Regions where data must be stored or processed, e.g. ["EU"]. Different from exit-IP countries.

detail.description: summary returns one source sentence per fact; full returns every recorded fact and sentence.

exit_ip_countries.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes of countries the page requests must exit from, e.g. ["US","DE"]. For search results of a country use search_countries.

failed_requests_not_billed.description: Requests that fail on the provider side (timeouts, blocks, 5xx) must not be billed. A flat monthly price for unlimited requests meets it, since no request is billed on its own; when only success-based billing will do, use only_successful_requests_billed.

limit.description: Maximum plans listed for each change and under confirm_with_provider (default 3).

max_monthly_cost_usd.description: Monthly budget in USD before tax. Compared with listed prices; annual plans use their per-month equivalent.

min_concurrency.description: Minimum number of concurrent requests (or browsers) the plan must allow.

min_pages_per_crawl.description: Pages one crawl job (from one start URL, following links) must be able to reach. A plan whose crawl has no page cap meets any number; give the size of the largest site to crawl. Different from the monthly page total.

min_requests_per_minute.description: Minimum request rate the plan must allow, per minute.

monthly_pages.description: Pages per month by type: plain_html (static pages), javascript (needs rendering), premium_proxy (blocked sites that need residential/premium proxies), javascript_premium_proxy (both).

monthly_pages_total.description: Total pages per month when the split by type is not known yet. Costs and verdicts then cover every share of JavaScript-rendered pages from 0% to 100% of the total (no premium proxies), and the result lists monthly_pages under needs_input.

monthly_searches.description: Search requests per month (one results page each).

needs_recurring_free_tier.description: The plan must be usable every month without paying (a free plan with a monthly allowance or a monthly free credit).

negotiable.description: Conditions the user said can change: monthly_volume, concurrency, rate_limit, monthly_budget, billing_type, free_allowance, failed_request_billing, success_billing, target_error_billing, geo_targeting, data_region, serp_response_mode, serp_localization, serp_result_types, serp_engines, crawl_page_limit. Default: every required condition, each marked ask_user because the user has not said it can change.

only_successful_requests_billed.description: Billing must count successful requests only: each successful request is charged (or draws credits) and failed ones cost nothing. A flat monthly price for unlimited requests does not meet it, since the price is the same whatever succeeds.

preferred.description: Nice-to-have conditions; they do not filter, they break ties.

realtime_search_required.description: Search results must be returned in real time (not through a queue).

search_countries.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes of the countries whose search results the searches must return (the search engine's country setting, e.g. Google gl), e.g. ["GB","CA"]. Different from exit_ip_countries.

search_engines.description: Search engines whose results the plan must return, each at the plan's search price: google, bing, yahoo, yandex, baidu, duckduckgo, naver, brave (brave is Brave's own index). monthly_searches is the total over all of them.

search_result_types.description: Result types the parsed search response must contain: organic, ads, local_pack, knowledge_graph, people_also_ask, related_searches, shopping, news, images, videos, ai_overview.

target_errors_not_billed.description: Error responses from the target site (e.g. 404) must not be billed.

product_types.description: Limit to these product types. Default: every type that can serve the workload.

When the fields must be found without writing selectors, use ai_extraction_pages instead; each page counts in one of the two.

target_errors_not_billed.description: Error responses from the target site (e.g. 404) must not be billed.

name: relax_conditions

ask_user.description: True when negotiable was not given: ask the user before changing this condition.

blocked_by.description: When no change of this condition alone is enough: other conditions not met by the plans that fail this one.

field.description: Request field of the condition; null for monthly_volume, which changes the workload fields.

facts.description: Official facts behind those verdicts (price facts are under monthly_cost).

also_stated_in.description: get_details only: other official machine-readable documents of the provider (llms.txt, llms-full.txt, OpenAPI files, MCP tool listings) that contain the same quoted sentences.

applies_to.description: get_details only: billing options (billing) or search engines (search_engines) the fact is limited to.

derived.description: How the value follows from the quoted sentence when it is not literal.

quote.description: The sentence as it appears on that page.

retrieved_at.description: Date the page was read (YYYY-MM-DD). Only with detail=full.

url.description: Official page the sentence was found on.

exceptions.description: get_details only: plans with a different value.

level.description: Where the fact is recorded: offer (the plan), product or provider.

status.description: TRUE: stated with the value; FALSE / NOT_SUPPORTED: stated as unavailable; UNKNOWN: not stated; CONFLICT: official pages disagree (value lists each version); STALE: past its recheck date; MISSING: not recorded.

via_exception.description: Present and true when a plan-specific exception replaced the general value.

meets_all.description: Against the request as given, before the change: false or "unknown".

meets_all_after_change.description: Against the request with this change applied: always true, because only plans that then meet every required condition are listed.
